items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: You played beside, you know, Eddie Durham and Panama I mentioned and Russell Procope

ctx.x: I don’t have a summation kind of thing, but I’m just again going back to something I wanted to say was I’m probably the luckiest person. You know some people say well there’s luck but there’s also this and that and being in the position to have luck or something like that. Nonetheless I am among the luckiest people that you’re ever going to interview.

All right. I consider myself pretty lucky too. And at one point I had had, because I was in the right place at the right time I got to ride to a gig with the Statesmen of Jazz, and like Milt Hinton was on my left, and he fell asleep on my shoulder. And I’m thinking, this is Milt Hinton and I’m with him, and Panama Francis and Claude Williams, and I’m just like, said to myself, you should really take note of this and appreciate it. So I’m wondering if you had that same feeling. You played beside, you know, Eddie…

To the degree that a 19-year-old can, or a 25-year-old. Yeah. I mean if you want to work biographically up to how all those things happened, so I’m back in New Jersey, you know, and I’m a teenager, and my parents are meeting some of these people and I’m hearing Teddy Wilson and then Hank Jones also was playing solo piano at a place called the Sherry Netherlands and I used to go there. My parents would leave me and Hank would drive me home. Was I appreciating it as to what it really was? How could I? I was 16…
